note: Task 17 does not rewrite the manuscript. No v0.3 was created.

changes.problem: The headline temporal deterioration is presented as a property of the 2019-2026 period; 89.3% of it comes from calendar 2020 and 2021 reverses sign.
changes.proposed_change: Add the per-year joint log-loss table with interval weights and contributions; state the ex-2020 residual (+0.00172) in the main text; qualify the abstract accordingly.

changes.problem: The unseen-vintage supplement reverses the sign of the protocol's primary decision metric and this is never reported.
changes.proposed_change: Report M1 0.070631 vs M2 0.069811 on 17,352 facilities with the cause-Brier counterpoint and the population differences; discuss what the reversal implies for the scope of the conclusion.

changes.problem: The payoff AUC gain is described as facility-level ranking; frozen per-year and CIF-level AUCs show it is between-period.
changes.proposed_change: Restate as across-period ranking; report the frozen 12 and 24-month CIF-level payoff AUCs (M1 0.5448/0.5906 vs M2 0.5442/0.5908); note that month-constant terms and prohibited interactions make a within-month gain structurally unavailable.

changes.problem: The calendar-block interval for the primary payoff Brier includes zero and is not reported, while the identical caveat is given for the exploratory result in section 8.
changes.proposed_change: Report [-4.738e-05, +0.013215] in section 6.4; lead with calendar-block intervals throughout; state that the frozen decision rule requires both intervals.

changes.problem: Only the 24-month CIF horizon is shown, which is the horizon at which M2 is worst; the 12-month horizon shows no qualitative failure.
changes.proposed_change: Show all four frozen horizons in one table; remove the CIF from the abstract as an independent finding and present it as the consequence of the monthly calibration result.

changes.problem: 'Historical rolling PIT paths' implies many entry dates; zero calendar truncation at 60 months implies entry is concentrated at the window start.
changes.proposed_change: Publish the landmark entry-month distribution; if concentrated, name the calendar span of the path and state that the CIF comparison and the 2020 calendar diagnostic are the same evidence.

changes.problem: 'Point-in-time' is used where frozen evidence records release lags as UNMEASURED for all six series.
changes.proposed_change: Replace with 'vintage-aware' or 'revision-aware', or define PIT explicitly as ALFRED vintage-date availability and state that provider release timestamps were not certified.

changes.problem: The weighting unit of the joint loss is never stated and no facility-weighted sensitivity exists.
changes.proposed_change: State equal interval weighting and its consequence (mean 44.3 intervals per facility; weighting correlated with the payoff outcome). Add a facility-weighted sensitivity or flag its absence as a limitation.

changes.problem: Joint log loss is the headline proper score but is ~98.4% no-event terms and barely separates M0 from M1.
changes.proposed_change: Demote joint log loss to one of several reported scores; promote cause-specific Brier and calibration; report the M0 comparison so the reader can see the metric's sensitivity.

changes.problem: Current delinquency state is excluded by design and the reader is not told that both models are origination-only.
changes.proposed_change: State in section 5.1 that no current-state covariate enters either model and that the macro increment conditional on current state is untested.

changes.problem: Every model under-predicts default CIF by roughly a factor of 3.4 at 24 months; only the payoff comparison is shown.
changes.proposed_change: Report the default CIF comparison beside the payoff one so the baseline's own failure is visible.

changes.problem: Support shift and coefficient instability are reported as separate observations; the sharper available statement is collinearity breakdown.
changes.proposed_change: State the development correlation structure (unemployment vs HPI growth -0.919, VIF 10-12, condition number 69.1, 88 distinct months) and the evaluation sign reversals as a single mechanism paragraph.

changes.problem: 'Temporal Transport' states the topic, not the finding, and overstates what a single provider and one macro excursion establish.
changes.proposed_change: Adopt a title naming the result and its scope, e.g. 'Vintage-aware macro features improve in-sample fit but not temporal probability quality in a seasoned Freddie Mac competing-risk cohort'.

changes.problem: Two paragraphs narrate the incompleteness of the authors' own literature search.
changes.proposed_change: Delete the search-completeness narration. Either obtain Bu2026 full text and fill the UNKNOWN cells, or state in one sentence that the closest comparison is unresolved.

changes.problem: Peng2026 lists macro conditioning and competing termination as future work and is the natural anchor; this is not used.
changes.proposed_change: Position the study in section 1 as the direct empirical answer to that stated open question.

changes.problem: 'Payoff' shorthand is defined once and then used unqualified in refinancing-flavoured sentences.
changes.proposed_change: Use 'payoff/maturity termination' on first use in each section, or add a one-line note that scheduled maturity is negligible for these vintages and terms.

changes.problem: 'Demonstrate' and the confirmatory register overstate a non-virgin frozen evaluation.
changes.proposed_change: Replace 'demonstrate' with 'record' or 'observe'; use 'frozen temporal evaluation', never 'confirmatory temporal validation'.

changes.problem: Caveat density buries the finding; most paragraphs retract the preceding sentence.
changes.proposed_change: Consolidate repeated caveats into section 10 and Table T8; state results and move.

changes.problem: A proposed-replication section and eight placeholder appendices read as unfinished.
changes.proposed_change: Reduce section 11 to two sentences in future work; remove appendix headers until content exists.

changes.problem: The XGBoost challenger result (AP 0.0175 vs 0.1763) is extreme enough to read as a configuration failure rather than a model-class finding.
changes.proposed_change: State the bounded configuration explicitly and avoid any implied comparison of model families; consider moving the comparison to a supplement.
